text: WHY NOT HIPPO? [no badge or logo text]
scene: A round-headed stick figure with furrowed brows pinches its nose and glances sideways between two plates on a lakeshore. The left plate holds a dark mottled-green hippo sliced to show a red cross-section above a grey-green steak with wavy stink lines; the right plate holds a cream-and-tan goat with a bright red cutaway above a fresh pink steak.
mechanism: A mirrored good-meat versus bad-meat pairing on identical plates, where the stink lines and rot colouring pose the question visually and the headline names the odd one out.
composition: The stick figure sits dead centre as a vertical divider with the hippo plate on the left and the goat plate on the right, giving near-symmetry. The headline takes the top fifth, the horizon line is low and calm, and both plates are about equal in scale so the eye has no single focal winner beyond the face.
typography: Three words in thick-outlined yellow capitals span almost the full width at the top, and HIPPO stays legible in the 160 render. The headline never says eat or meat, so the plates carry that idea while the title adds it in words.
colors: Saturated sky blue over grass green frames a yellow headline for strong pop. Semantic colour is used on the plates: murky green-brown for the hippo, warm cream and pink for the goat.
psychology: The pinched nose and sideways stare read as disgust or doubt, and the wavy odour lines add a smell cue. All signals are cartoon cues; no real person is shown.
partnership: The title supplies the missing verb eat and the word never, while the thumbnail shortens it to a bare question about hippo. The green decay on the hippo plate hints at the answer, which may spend some curiosity before the click.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the stick figure's pinched-nose face, then the stinking hippo plate on the left, then the goat plate for contrast.
art: Flat 2D vector doodle with consistent outline weight and clean fills. The hippo being sliced in half like a roast is surreal but internally coherent, and the background is simple so everything holds up at 160x90.
strength: Two matching plates make the contrast readable in a glance.
weakness: The rot colouring leaks the likely answer, and the headline omits the word eat.
bottleneck: Viewers must infer the eating question from the plates because the headline alone is ambiguous.
action: Hypothesis: test the headline WHY NOT EAT HIPPO? against the current wording to see whether naming the action sharpens the question.
counterexample: Seq 15 uses the same two-plate layout but spells EAT in its headline.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: MONEY IS / EVERYTHING [no badge or logo text]
scene: A large egg-headed cartoon man with a scowl and open shouting mouth points a finger at a small grey safe sitting on a wooden table. The safe door is open and shows a banded stack of green bills, and a hand-drawn black curved arrow sweeps down to it from the headline. The background is plain white.
mechanism: An absolute, unhedged claim stated in huge type while a cartoon figure literally points at the cash, pairing a bold opinion with a concrete money object.
composition: The headline block fills the top right and the man fills the left third, making a left-to-right diagonal down to the safe. The safe is the lower-right secondary focus. White negative space keeps three elements separated with almost no clutter.
typography: Two lines of heavy black condensed capitals, three words in total, occupy about half the frame. Contrast on white is maximal and the words are fully readable at 160x90. The text restates the title's idea more bluntly and adds no new fact.
colors: Near-black headline on pure white with a small green accent from the cash and light blue shirt. Colour is minimal, so the single green block stands out as the money signal.
psychology: The shouting mouth and narrowed eyes read as argumentative or insistent, which suits a provocative claim. Nothing signals warning or hope beyond the cartoon expression.
partnership: The title hedges with Matters More Than We're Willing to Admit, while the thumbnail drops the hedge to flat Money Is Everything, which escalates the claim. The unanswered question is why the creator holds that view.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: huge headline first, then the arrow's tail, then the open safe and cash, and last the angry man's face on the left.
art: Clean flat vector with thick outlines and a smooth gradient on the safe. The man's head is one oversized egg shape on a thin neck, stylised rather than anatomically odd, and the layout stays crisp on mobile.
strength: Maximum-contrast headline lets the claim land even at 160x90.
weakness: The finger-pointing man and safe are generic stock-style props that give no specific angle.
bottleneck: Distinctiveness is low because the same white-background mascot-plus-arrow template is common in this niche.
action: Hypothesis: replace the generic safe with a visual that contradicts the claim, such as the same cash stack beside a small non-money object, to test whether tension lifts interest.
counterexample: Seq 14 pairs a similar bold black headline with a distressed character so the emotion carries the idea.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: UTIS IN / MEMORY LOSS / & NURSING / HOMES [Leslie Kernisan, MD MPH] [Chrissy Kistler, MD MASc]
scene: Two video-call tiles sit on the right: the upper shows a smiling woman with dark curly hair against a plain white wall, the lower a laughing woman with grey-blonde hair in a mustard top in a cluttered room. Each tile carries a printed name and credential caption. A small circular line-drawing logo of two walking figures, one with a cane, sits top left.
mechanism: Named-expert video panel with a plain topic headline, signalling a doctor conversation rather than creating a curiosity gap.
composition: Headline stacks down the left two-thirds in four lines while two rounded call tiles stack on the right. The balance is clean but the text and tiles compete for focus, and the large empty teal margins add no depth.
typography: Four stacked lines with six headline words: UTIS IN MEMORY LOSS in black and & NURSING HOMES in white. The black-on-teal contrast is good, the white lines are weaker, and the small name captions are unreadable at 160x90. The headline restates the title and adds only the phrase nursing homes.
colors: A flat mint-teal background carries black and white type with pale tiles. Saturation is moderate and the palette feels calm and clinical, with no warning or alarm colours.
psychology: Both guests are visibly smiling or laughing, which signals warmth, approachability and low alarm. The credential captions give authority cues, and the nursing homes phrase touches caregiver concern.
partnership: The thumbnail repeats the title topic and adds nursing homes but no question, number or consequence. The only unanswered thing is whether UTIs cause memory problems, which stays implicit.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black headline first, then the white NURSING HOMES lines, then the upper smiling face tile, then the lower tile; the tiny logo is skipped.
art: Screenshot-style composition from a recorded call with rounded-corner tiles on a flat fill. Lighting and framing differ between the two webcams, which is natural for a call and not an editing artefact.
strength: Visible MD credentials and relaxed faces give a credible, calm expert-interview cue.
weakness: The headline names a topic only, with no tension, stakes or specific takeaway.
bottleneck: Low emotional urgency leaves clicking to depend on prior interest in the subject.
action: Hypothesis: replace the second headline line with a concrete stake, for example a single question about confusion in older adults, and enlarge one expert face to test the effect.
counterexample: Seq 10 does the opposite by using a red alarm palette and a large single clinician face for urgency.
medical_notes: Printed MD credentials and a plain topic headline make no cure or diagnosis claim, though the video content is unchecked.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: BLACK LIFE THEN? / ANCIENT / KINGDOMS / COLONIAL / MODERN
scene: A worried stick figure with a raised eyebrow rests a hand on its chin at the left, looking at a four-panel timeline. The panels show a figure in a white toga labelled ANCIENT, a figure in a crown and purple robe labelled KINGDOMS, a stick figure in chains labelled COLONIAL, and a figure in a grey suit and tie labelled MODERN. All the era figures have brown heads.
mechanism: A compact four-era timeline lets the viewer scan history as a sequence, with a skeptical observer adding a curiosity beat.
composition: Headline spans the top and the framed timeline takes the right two-thirds, while the stick observer stands at the left edge. Panels are evenly divided and read left to right, a strong ordered structure with the observer as a secondary focus.
typography: Seven words in two tiers: a large yellow outlined BLACK LIFE THEN? and small black era labels in a white strip. The headline survives at 160x90 but the era labels are too small to read. The headline compresses the title's history framing and the labels add the four eras.
colors: Tan-beige base with a yellow headline and pastel panel backgrounds in yellow, tan, blue and green. Costume colours (white, purple, grey) give each era its own accent, and overall saturation is moderate.
psychology: The observer's skeptical eyebrow and chin-hand pose signal puzzlement. The chained figure in the third panel is a stark trauma cue, but the rest is neutral. The cues are cartoon signals only.
partnership: The thumbnail extends the title with a visible four-era structure of ancient, kingdoms, colonial and modern. It shows the span of the answer without revealing details, so the main open question is what each era was like.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline, then the crowned figure in panel two, then the chained figure in panel three, then the observer stick figure, with era labels last.
art: Flat vector with a consistent doodle style, even outlines and clearly separated panels. The simplified brown-headed figures stay readable but the labels collapse at small size.
strength: The four-panel timeline gives an immediate structure of what the video covers.
weakness: The era labels vanish at 160x90 and the figures are very similar in scale and head shape.
bottleneck: Most of the information sits in the tiny label row that disappears on mobile.
action: Hypothesis: crop to two contrasting panels (crown and chains) at double size to test whether fewer, larger scenes beat the four-label timeline.
counterexample: Seq 19 also uses a labelled scene but relies on two large objects rather than small captions.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: JUST / STRESS? [no badge or logo text]
scene: SHORTS: the actual artwork is a vertical card centred on blurred brown-red side bars. It shows an older man in a grey polo climbing stairs with his hand on his chest, which has a red glow, and in front a bearded man with glasses in blue scrubs gestures with an open palm and looks toward the camera. The stairwell is dim with a metal railing.
mechanism: A rhetorical question that dismisses a symptom, set against a visible chest-clutching figure, creates a tension between 'just stress' and an apparent cardiac warning.
composition: The vertical artwork has JUST STRESS? in the top third, the distressed man at mid-left and the bearded man at lower right, forming a diagonal. The side bars waste about two thirds of the 16:9 frame, so the active subject is small.
typography: Two words in huge condensed type: white JUST over red STRESS?. Contrast on the dark background is strong, but the whole card is only about a third of the frame width, so letters are small at 160x90. The headline repeats the anxiety half of the title and omits heart attack.
colors: A dark navy-black card with white and red type, a red glow on the chest and blue scrubs. The blurred brown-red side bars are a muted, unrelated colour field. Red is used semantically for stress and the symptom.
psychology: The older man's wide eyes and pained posture signal fear and vulnerability, while the other man's open palm and direct stare read as explanatory authority. The red chest glow is a visual alarm cue.
partnership: The title poses Chest Pressure or Anxiety? and promises warning signs; the thumbnail keeps only the stress side and shows the symptom. The open question is how to tell stress from a heart attack, with no answer revealed.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: white JUST, then red STRESS?, then the glowing red chest, then the bearded man's face and gesture; the side bars are ignored.
art: Photoreal-looking render with a shallow dark gradient. The red chest glow is overlaid and clearly graphical. The vertical artwork is centred on blurred bars, which makes the main art tiny in a landscape slot.
strength: Red-over-white stacked headline plus a glowing chest makes the stress-versus-heart question instantly clear.
weakness: Only about a third of the frame carries content, shrinking everything on mobile.
bottleneck: Vertical artwork in a landscape slot leaves the readable area narrow and small.
action: Hypothesis: fill the landscape frame with a re-cropped version of the chest and headline instead of blurred side bars to test legibility gains.
counterexample: Seq 10 fills the whole 16:9 frame with its clinician and alarm graphics, making its subject far larger.
medical_notes: The man in blue scrubs has no printed name or credential, and the thumbnail frames chest pain as possibly just stress without content to confirm the guidance.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: Kill or / Die [lost legacy logo]
scene: A close-up ninja in a dark navy hood and mask with a red headband grips his head with both hands, brows furrowed, eyes wide and welling with tears, and sweat drops flying around. A sword hilt wrapped in red sticks out behind his shoulder. A thin hand-drawn arrow at the right points back toward him next to the handwritten words.
mechanism: A tearful, panicking ninja next to the stakes phrase 'Kill or Die' makes the headline and the emotion do the story work together.
composition: The ninja fills the left 60 percent with his face as the dominant focal point, while handwritten text sits in a wide empty white area on the right. The arrow connects text to character, and the logo sits tiny in the top left.
typography: Three handwritten-style words in thin black strokes on white; the text is medium in size and low in weight compared with the illustration. At 160x90 it is faintly readable but lighter than the figure. It adds the stakes that the title (why it sucked) only implies.
colors: White background with dark navy-indigo clothing, red headband and trim, and light blue tear drops. Contrast between the dark character and white background is high, and red marks the ninja identity.
psychology: Tears, sweat and clutched head signal fear and overwhelm, a vulnerability cue the viewer may want explained. The framing is a visible-emotion cue, not proof of the video's content.
partnership: The thumbnail adds the stakes (kill or die) that the title Why It Sucked to Be a Ninja leaves open, showing the sucked part as terror. It does not reveal a specific incident, so the question what actually happened remains.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: crying eyes and furrowed brow first, then the red headband, then the handwritten Kill or Die, then the arrow back.
art: Hand-inked comic style with variable line weight and flat colour fills. The hands are anatomically consistent with five fingers each, shading is simple, and the white background keeps it clean and mobile-friendly.
strength: The panicked, crying face gives a strong emotional hook.
weakness: The thin handwriting is much weaker than the dark figure and may be missed on a phone.
bottleneck: The text is the lowest-contrast element, while all the weight sits on the character.
action: Hypothesis: thicken the words and put Kill or Die in a bold outlined face to see whether text visibility improves.
counterexample: Seq 21 does the opposite with heavy black type that dominates over its faces.
hero_object: crying ninja with hands on head
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: ALMOST AT / $1,000,000 [no badge or logo text]
scene: A smug egg-headed cartoon man with half-lidded eyes and a closed-mouth smile stands with arms crossed at the left, ankle-deep in a field of green coins. A red alarm clock sits among the coins at centre. A thick black arrow from the dollar figure curves down to that clock. The background above the coins is plain white.
mechanism: A large, specific number with an alarm clock next to it creates a countdown feeling, with a smug cartoon figure showing near-completion.
composition: The dollar figure dominates the upper right as the primary point and the arrow pulls the eye down to the clock at the lower centre. The man anchors the left, and the coin mounds along the bottom form a green base. Spacing is clear and uncluttered.
typography: Three words: ALMOST AT in large bold black caps, about 60% of the height of the giant $1,000,000 beneath it, tightly set. Contrast on white is maximal and the number reads at 160x90. The title adds the one-third math and the surprising angle that the thumbnail leaves out.
colors: White background, black type, a green coin field and a red clock accent. The green connotes money and the red clock supplies urgency, giving clean accent separation.
psychology: The smug, relaxed pose reads as confidence rather than anxiety. The red alarm clock adds a time-pressure cue, but the cartoon's calm face softens it.
partnership: The title says $100,000 is a third of the way to $1,000,000, while the thumbnail says almost at $1,000,000, which is on-face tension. The open question is how close and in how long, which the clock hints without answering.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the giant $1,000,000 first, then the arrow to the red clock, then the smug face on the left, then the coin pile.
art: Flat vector with consistent line weight and a tidy white field. The coins are uniform and the pile edge is repeated, which reads as a vector fill. It is crisp and remains legible on mobile.
strength: The giant number plus red clock delivers an instant stakes-and-time idea.
weakness: Almost at contradicts the title's one-third framing, so the promise can feel inconsistent.
bottleneck: Smug man and white void add little beyond the number, so the number carries nearly all the information.
action: Hypothesis: replace ALMOST AT with 1/3 AT in the same type and compare to see whether matching the title increases perceived honesty.
counterexample: Seq 11 uses the identical mascot and arrow template but states a rule instead of a countdown.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: YOU QUIT. [no badge or logo text]
scene: A big-headed cartoon worker in a navy cap, dark jacket and orange hi-vis vest strolls toward the left, smirking and waving over his shoulder. Behind him in a warm-lit warehouse, a red-faced supervisor in a hard hat points and yells while holding a clipboard aloft, flanked by two shocked colleagues in yellow helmets clutching their cheeks. A red arrow points to the walker's head from the headline, and a faint sparkle logo shows in the lower right.
mechanism: A wish-fulfilment POV scene where the viewer is the one walking away while an enraged boss and panicking colleagues react behind.
composition: The walker is the primary focal point on the left and the angry boss with colleagues form a secondary cluster at the right, creating a left-versus-right split. The headline floats at the top centre with an arrow tying it to the walker. The warehouse shelves add depth but also clutter.
typography: Two white capitalised words with a black outline and a full stop sit at the top centre. Contrast against the warm-lit background is moderate but holds, and it survives at 160x90. The text uses second-person POV that the title does not directly state.
colors: Warm amber and orange lighting dominates, with the blue cap and red boss face as accents. The orange hi-vis and shelf tones can blend with the background, so separation relies on dark outlines.
psychology: The relaxed smile and wave signal confidence and relief, while the yelling boss and frightened coworkers signal conflict and consequence. The 'you' address invites self-projection.
partnership: The title is about saving $3 a day and never worrying about money, while the thumbnail is about quitting a job. The link between them is not shown on the thumbnail, so the on-face relation is weak.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: white YOU QUIT. first, then the walker's smirking face via the red arrow, then the red-faced boss, then the shocked colleagues.
art: Rendered cartoon with soft gradients and defined outlines. The walker's head is oversized relative to the body and the hands are plausible. Lighting from the left glow is consistent and the background is busy but secondary.
strength: A clear who-leaves, who-reacts story reads in one glance.
weakness: Warm orange scene and many small figures reduce subject separation.
bottleneck: The thumbnail's quit-the-job narrative does not mention money, so the title's saving angle is disconnected.
action: Hypothesis: add a small dollar or savings symbol near the walker to test whether tying the exit to money improves title-thumbnail fit.
counterexample: Seq 16 shares the headline and template but uses a cooler, less cluttered office.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: ENTIRE CITIES GONE? [no badge or logo text]
scene: A shaggy-haired caveman stick figure kneels at the right edge, mouth open in alarm and eyes wide, holding a grey stone tile. A large slab with six circular recesses fills the centre; only the top-left recess holds a tiny walled town with a columned temple and red-roofed houses, while the other five are empty beige hollows.
mechanism: A slab with one city left and five empty slots visualises disappearance as a missing-pieces puzzle, with the alarmed caveman holding the last tile.
composition: The slab runs diagonally across the centre and left with the kneeling figure at the lower right, so the eye moves from the filled slot at top-left across the empty ones to the figure. The headline sits above in a clean band. Negative space inside the slots is intentional.
typography: Three words in thick-outlined yellow capitals across the full width. Legibility at 160x90 is solid. The headline gives the stakes the title only implies (cities vanishing) and omits the number 6 that the title includes.
colors: Warm tan background and grey slab with a yellow headline as the only saturated colour. The tiny town with red roofs on a green circular base is the one colourful accent among beige slots, which draws attention to the lone survivor.
psychology: The caveman's wide eyes and open mouth read as shock or dismay, supporting a loss and mystery mood. The empty slots communicate absence without any graphic imagery.
partnership: The title asks how the other 6 civilizations disappeared, while the picture shows one city plus five empty slots, so the count does not visibly match six. The open question of why they vanished is clear but the headline reveals nothing about the cause.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the single lit town at top-left, then the row of empty hollows, then the shocked caveman.
art: Flat vector doodle with a slightly sketchy outline and subtle texture on the grey slab. The perspective on the slab is believable, the hands hold the tile plausibly, and the empty background keeps mobile legibility high.
strength: One filled slot among five empty ones makes the missing-civilisation idea instantly visual.
weakness: The town icon that carries the concept shrinks to a few pixels at 160x90; the slab has six recesses (one filled, five empty), so the counting cue is clear only on a larger view.
bottleneck: The only detail carrying the whole concept, the tiny town, is small at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the town and add one more faint outline to the empty slots to test whether the missing-pieces idea reads faster.
counterexample: Seq 12 shows a joyful figure with a large animal and leaves no unresolved gap.
hero_object: six-hollow stone slab with one city
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: WAKE UP AT / 3 AM? / YOUR HEART IS WARNING YOU / [3:00 AM clock]
scene: Split frame: on the right a grey-bearded man in navy scrubs with a stethoscope presses a finger beneath his eye and stares at the camera against a deep red background. On the left, a black panel holds the text and an inset showing a bedside digital clock reading 3:00 AM beside a glowing translucent heart with a red lightning-bolt crack, outlined by a yellow frame and pointed to by a small red arrow.
mechanism: A time-of-night trigger linked by arrow to a cracked heart, with a clinician-style figure pointing at his eye, packages a fear-based health warning.
composition: A diagonal white divider splits the frame, with text and the inset on the left and the large face on the right. The man's face is the dominant focal point and the inset clock-and-heart is the secondary zone, but four text and graphic layers make the left side crowded.
typography: Ten words on three tiers: yellow WAKE UP AT, giant white outlined 3 AM?, and white-on-red banner YOUR HEART IS WARNING YOU. The first two tiers survive at 160x90 while the banner shrinks. The thumbnail adds a heart claim that the title (often after 60) does not state.
colors: Black and deep red with yellow and white type and a red glow on the heart. Saturation and contrast are very high, and red is used semantically for danger.
psychology: The wide stare, raised finger at the eye and red palette signal alarm and urgency. The scrubs and stethoscope borrow clinical authority, and the cracked heart is a fear cue aimed at older viewers.
partnership: The title is a neutral address to people over 60, while the thumbnail escalates to a direct claim that the heart is warning you. The unanswered question is whether waking at 3 AM really signals heart trouble, which the image asserts rather than asks.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow WAKE UP AT, then the giant white 3 AM?, then the staring face on the right, then the red banner, then the clock and cracked heart inset.
art: Polished composite with a clean cutout of the man against the red gradient, a stylised glowing heart and a dark bedside render. The pointing finger and eyes look natural, and lighting on the man and the red backdrop is consistent. It is dense but strong in poster form.
strength: Specific time cue plus a red-banner claim and large human face grab attention hard.
weakness: The red banner and the small inset are crowded and the heart claim is unsupported on-face.
bottleneck: Four stacked text-and-graphic layers compete on the left, so the second tier overshadows the claim banner.
action: Hypothesis: drop the inset and keep only 3 AM? plus the face to test whether a simpler frame lifts mobile readability.
counterexample: Seq 3 uses calm teal and relaxed faces with a topic-only headline, the opposite of this alarm styling.
expression_label: direct alarmed stare with finger at eye
hero_object: cracked glowing heart beside 3:00 AM clock
medical_notes: The banner asserts that waking at 3 AM means your heart is warning you, with a cracked-heart image and a figure in scrubs carrying no printed name or credential.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: THE / $20,000 / RULE [no badge or logo text]
scene: A cartoon man with a large egg-shaped head and rust-coloured hair, half-lidded eyes and a faint smirk, wears a blue hoodie and points toward a grey steel safe. Beside the safe lies a stack of banded green bills. A thick black curved arrow from the word RULE sweeps down to the cash on a plain white background.
mechanism: A named financial threshold framed as a rule with a safe and cash stack makes a specific figure feel like a secret formula.
composition: The stacked text fills the right half and the figure with the safe fills the left half, balanced as two blocks. The arrow forms a loop from RULE down to the cash, and the pointing arm directs attention to the safe. White space keeps the layout uncluttered.
typography: Three words in massive black capitals over three lines, with $20,000 largest. Contrast and weight are the highest in this batch, and the number reads at 160x90. The title adds the idea that things change even more after the amount, which the thumbnail omits.
colors: Black on white with grey safe, blue hoodie and green cash accents. The palette is restrained and the green banknotes are the only strong colour point.
psychology: The smirk and half-lidded eyes suggest confidence and smug authority rather than worry. There is no visible fear or hope signal, only a calm-claim tone.
partnership: The title says everything changes even more after $20,000, while the thumbnail packages it as a rule, giving a more compact claim. What the rule is remains unanswered, which creates curiosity.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: giant $20,000 first, then the word RULE and the arrow down to the cash stack, then the safe, then the smirking face.
art: Crisp flat vector with a gentle shading on the safe door and bill stack. The man's pointing arm is a bit stiff and the head shape is a repeating mascot form, but there are no visible artefacts and it is very clean on mobile.
strength: Top-tier legibility, with a giant number and an arrow to a concrete cash image.
weakness: The face is expressionless and the safe prop is generic.
bottleneck: The mascot's neutral smirk adds almost no emotion beyond the number.
action: Hypothesis: give the figure a surprised or doubtful expression to test whether emotion beside the number raises appeal.
counterexample: Seq 7 uses a nearly identical mascot but adds a clock to convey time pressure.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: PET EVERYTHING [no badge or logo text]
scene: A grinning shaggy-haired caveman stick figure kneels on grass and scratches the chin of a large orange saber-toothed cat that lies with eyes closed and a contented smile. The big cat's long white fangs are visible. Rolling green hills, stone huts and a small campfire sit behind under a light blue sky.
mechanism: Reversing the expected predator-prey fear by showing a human happily cuddling a dangerous animal, so the surprise itself is the hook.
composition: The saber-toothed cat occupies the left and centre as the largest mass and the caveman's face sits at upper right, with their heads close together as the key interaction. Headline spans the top but the caveman's hair overlaps the lower edge of the letters G and N.
typography: Two words in yellow outlined capitals with extra letter-spacing along the top; legible at 160x90. The caveman's hair covers part of the final letters and the title's mention of ancient reasons is left out.
colors: Blue sky, green hills, orange cat and tan caveman clothing form a bright saturated palette. The yellow headline fits the same cheerful family, and cat orange separates well from the green.
psychology: The caveman's wide grin and the cat's closed-eye smile signal joy, trust and affection. The visible fangs add a faint danger undercurrent that makes the friendliness surprising.
partnership: The title asks about the ancient reason why humans cannot resist petting everything, and the thumbnail mirrors it with PET EVERYTHING. The picture hints at an ancient link via caveman and fangs but states no reason, leaving the why open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow PET EVERYTHING first, then the caveman's grinning face, then the cat's blissful closed eyes and fangs.
art: Flat vector with a hand-drawn wobble and warm shading on the cat. The stick-figure arms reach the chin plausibly and the overall composition is coherent. The background is lightly detailed, and the lettering overlap is the only visible flaw.
strength: The friendly saber-tooth makes a vivid, memorable image with a built-in surprise.
weakness: The caveman's hair crowds the tail of the headline letters.
bottleneck: The picture is a pleasant gag but shows no explanatory hook for why.
action: Hypothesis: shift the headline left or lower the caveman by a few pixels so no letters are overlapped, then compare readability.
counterexample: Seq 18 shows the same predator subject in a tense, dark night mood rather than friendly.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: REMOVE 20 LBS OF WASTE [no badge or logo text]
scene: A yellow banner above a split frame. On the left a glass jar with a green lid holds golden liquid full of black seeds with a dense layer settled at the bottom, set against a blurred high-rise window view. On the right a glossy rendering of a pink large intestine shows brown lumpy matter inside, a yellow arrow pointing at a segment and a magnifying glass enlarging it, against a dark clinical background.
mechanism: A home remedy jar placed next to an exaggerated colon full of waste implies the drink removes bulk, packaging a miracle detox as a before-and-after causal pair.
composition: The yellow headline bar spans the top and two equal panels split the rest, creating symmetry. The jar and intestine are both full-height focal elements, and the yellow arrow and magnifier mark the zoom point. The panels are busy and dense with textures.
typography: Five words in heavy black capitals on a solid yellow bar fill the width and stay legible at 160x90. The bar is the cleanest part of the frame. The title adds the $3 oil, overnight timing and belly fat claim that the thumbnail omits.
colors: Yellow banner, amber liquid with black seeds, and saturated pink-red and brown intestine give a high-saturation, high-contrast palette. Brown matter reads as waste, and the yellow arrow flags the problem spot.
psychology: The graphic waste imagery targets disgust and fear that something is lodged inside, and the number 20 LBS suggests a dramatic result. There are no faces; the signal is purely visceral.
partnership: The title names a $3 oil and overnight flushing, while the thumbnail shows a seed-filled liquid and a waste-loaded colon with no oil visible. The open question is what the product is, and the picture asserts a large-scale effect as fact.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black-on-yellow REMOVE 20 LBS OF WASTE first, then the lumpy colon on the right, then the seed-filled jar, then the arrow and magnifier.
art: Photoreal-style jar and a glossy rendered colon with synthetic lighting that looks rendered rather than photographed. The colon's smooth, oversized lumps are anatomically implausible, and the two panels have unrelated backgrounds, with no shared lighting.
strength: The yellow banner is highly legible and the two-panel before-style pairing is quick to parse.
weakness: Anatomically exaggerated waste imagery and an unqualified 20 LBS claim are unsupported.
bottleneck: The product, the oil, is not visible, so the claim has no identifiable cause.
action: Hypothesis: replace the 20 LBS claim with a question about the jar and show the oil bottle to test a less absolute framing.
counterexample: Seq 3 makes no health claim and uses a calm credentialed layout.
medical_notes: The thumbnail claims a specific 20 lb waste removal and shows an exaggerated impacted colon rendering with no clinical context, which is an unsupported treatment claim.

text: MILLIONAIRES / AFRAID / TO RETIRE

composition: The figure occupies the left quarter as a tall narrow focal point and the three-line headline fills the right. The briefcase of cash is the secondary object and the plain white void keeps it clean. The balance is left-heavy with strong text mass at right.
typography: Four words across three heavy black lines, with TO RETIRE on a yellow highlight bar. Contrast is maximal and the lines survive at 160x90. The title adds the explanation that money cannot fix this, which the thumbnail leaves out.
colors: Black on white with a yellow highlight bar and a muted charcoal suit, plus green banknotes and a brown case as small accents. The yellow marks the key phrase.
psychology: Sweat, wide eyes and an open mouth signal anxiety. Tightly clutching the money bag adds a fear-of-losing cue.
partnership: The title says millionaires are afraid to retire and that money cannot fix it, while the thumbnail restates the fear with almost the same words. It leaves why unanswered but supplies the same phrase twice.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: black MILLIONAIRES first, then the yellow-highlighted TO RETIRE, then the sweating face, then the spilling cash bag.
art: Clean vector illustration with uniform line weight; the grey-bearded character is drawn coherently. The hands gripping the case and the sweat drop are coherent, and nothing is cut off, so it is crisp on mobile.
strength: Paradox of a rich, frightened man is instantly legible with large text and a clear emotional face.
weakness: The thumbnail duplicates the title's wording and offers no extra mystery.
bottleneck: Because the headline repeats the title, the picture bears all added value.

text: EAT YOUR PET? [no badge or logo text]
scene: A stick figure with a pale round head and wide worried eyes covers its mouth with one hand between two plates on a green savannah with acacia trees. The left plate holds a black-and-white cow sliced open with three fresh red steaks; the right plate holds a sad golden dog split with a mouldy green interior, three dark spoiled steaks and wavy stink lines.
mechanism: A cow-versus-dog plate pair with rot only on the pet side makes the taboo concrete and ties it to the disgust of the observer.
composition: The stick figure's face is centred with a plate on each side, a near-mirror layout with the headline across the top. The dog's sad face is a strong secondary focal point, and the acacia trees add depth without cluttering.
typography: Three words in thick-outlined yellow capitals at the top centre, legible at 160x90. The headline states the taboo directly, while the title adds the broader never-eat framing.
colors: Bright blue sky and saturated green grass behind a yellow headline. The cow's fresh red steaks contrast with the dog's olive-green decay, and that semantic colour split is the core of the picture.
psychology: The covered mouth and wide eyes signal revulsion and shock, and the dog's downturned eyes add sympathy. The cues are cartoon expressions only.
partnership: The title asks why we never eat our own pet animals, while the thumbnail asks EAT YOUR PET, a provocative short form. The rotted dog meat hints at one answer without explaining it.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow EAT YOUR PET? first, then the stick figure's covered mouth, then the green-rotted dog plate, then the clean cow plate.
art: Flat vector with consistent outlines and soft shading. The dog and cow are split in the same cut-through way, which looks deliberate. The scene is simple and survives at 160x90.
strength: The taboo question is crisp and the cow-versus-dog contrast is quickly decoded.
weakness: The green rot colouring on the dog side leaks the disgust answer.
bottleneck: The strongest hook, the dog's sad face, is smaller than the figure at centre.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the dog's face and trim the stink lines to test whether sympathy lifts the emotional pull.
counterexample: Seq 1 uses the same layout but without the pet taboo, so it is less provocative.

text: YOU QUIT. [no badge or logo text]

A red arrow from the headline points to his head. To the right in a cold grey-blue office, a red-faced man in a navy suit points and shouts while two colleagues hold their heads in alarm behind desks and a bin.
mechanism: A warm-versus-cold split shows the walker leaving into light while a furious boss and stressed staff remain in the grey, framing quitting as emotional victory.
composition: The walker is the tall primary focal point at left and the shouting boss is a clear secondary figure at right. The headline sits at the top centre with an arrow looping to the walker. The light-to-dark split gives a diagonal depth and moderate clutter.
typography: Two white capitalised words with black outline and a full stop at the top centre. The blue ceiling lights partly merge with the letters but it still survives at 160x90. The title's nobody-noticed angle is absent from the text.
colors: Warm gold light on the left versus cool grey-blue on the right, with a red arrow and red boss face as focal accents. The colour split carries the story of exit versus misery.
psychology: The calm smile and brisk walk signal relief and freedom, while the shouting boss and clutching staff signal stress. The 'you' address invites self-projection.
partnership: The title says You Escaped the Rat Race and Nobody Noticed, but the thumbnail shows a loud boss and colleagues visibly reacting, which is on-face tension. The thumbnail answers the quitting part and ignores the nobody-noticed part.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: white YOU QUIT. first, then the red arrow to the walker, then the red-faced boss in the cold office, then the head-clutching colleagues.
art: Cartoon render with soft gradients and sun-ray light on the left. Perspective of the ceiling and desks is consistent and the cold-versus-warm light split is plausible. Slight head-to-body scale exaggeration is stylistic.
strength: Warm-versus-cold lighting makes the leave-the-misery story obvious.
weakness: Reaction of the boss contradicts the title's claim that nobody noticed.
bottleneck: The title and the picture disagree on whether anyone reacted.
action: Hypothesis: show colleagues ignoring the walker with blank faces to test whether matching the title's nobody-noticed idea improves fit.
counterexample: Seq 8 uses the same headline in a warehouse and is busier, with weaker subject separation.

text: HOW MANY SURVIVORS? [no badge or logo text]
scene: Seven stick-figure people stand along the curve of a brown continental globe against a blue sky and a skyline of blue apartment blocks. Most have flat, neutral faces; a woman in a purple dress holds a swaddled baby with a worried look, and the central figure with brown hair looks anxious while holding a clipboard labelled POPULATION with a row of zeros ending in B.
mechanism: A tiny group standing on top of the whole planet turns a population-minimum question into a vivid last-survivors tableau, with a clipboard counter as the data prop.
composition: The semicircle of Earth anchors the bottom and the seven figures form an arc along its top edge. The headline spans the top and the clipboard at centre-right is the secondary focus. The city silhouettes at both sides frame the group, with moderate figure density.
typography: Three words in thick yellow outlined capitals across the top; legible at 160x90. The clipboard text POPULATION is readable only at native size and the zeros are tiny. The title adds repopulating Earth and smallest, which the headline omits.
colors: Strong blue sky with a tan-brown globe and yellow headline. Figures use muted jacket colours, and the single purple dress marks the baby carrier as a secondary accent.
psychology: Neutral faces read as blank, while the woman's and clipboard-holder's worried eyes signal fear. The baby adds vulnerability and stakes.
partnership: The title asks for the smallest population needed to repopulate Earth, and the thumbnail asks how many survivors, which is a shorter, apocalypse-flavoured version. The count is the unanswered question, and no number is shown in a readable way.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow headline first, then the woman with the baby, then the anxious clipboard holder, then the row of flat-faced figures and the globe.
art: Flat vector with consistent outlines and tidy proportions. The figures follow the globe curve with plausible footing, and the zero-filled clipboard text has smudged glyphs that read as generic filler rather than a real number.
strength: Seven small people on a huge globe turns an abstract count into an instant picture.
weakness: Many similar figures with small, neutral faces dilute the emotional focus.
bottleneck: The clipboard number, the data hook, is illegible at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: cut the group to three figures and a single large numeral to test whether a readable count beats a crowd.
counterexample: Seq 18 uses two large animals with one clear tension instead of a crowd.

hero_object: clipboard on top of the globe

text: WHY NOT ATTACK? [no badge or logo text]
scene: At night, an orange-and-black striped tiger prowls left to right in a dark grassy field with its yellow eyes locked ahead, while a black-and-white zebra lies curled asleep at the right with its head tucked down. A white crescent moon sits in the upper right over dark teal hills and a bare tree at the left.
mechanism: A predator walking toward an apparently defenceless sleeper builds suspense, and the headline asks the contrary question of why it holds back.
composition: The tiger takes the left and centre as the primary mass and the sleeping zebra sits right as the second focal point, creating a left-to-right movement. The headline spans the top and the moon balances the upper right corner. The dark palette helps the orange tiger stand out.
typography: Three words in big yellow outlined capitals across the top, with strong contrast on the dark teal sky; legible at 160x90. The headline mirrors the title and does not add detail.
colors: Dark teal and near-black night palette with an orange tiger and yellow headline as the only vivid accents. The black-and-white zebra stands out as a pale shape against the dark ground.
psychology: The tiger's fixed yellow stare reads as predatory focus and the zebra's curled posture reads as vulnerable. The night setting adds tension without gore.
partnership: The title asks why predators do not attack sleeping prey, and the thumbnail pictures exactly that moment. It hands over the setup but nothing about the reason, so the gap is clear.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow WHY NOT ATTACK? first, then the tiger's eyes and head, then the sleeping zebra, then the moon.
art: Vector with textured shading on the dark background and crisp outlines on the animals. Stripe patterns on both animals are consistent and the lighting suggests moonlight. The darker palette still survives at 160x90.
strength: Dark background makes the orange tiger and yellow headline pop, and the scene sets up a clear dilemma.
weakness: Only the tiger's face carries emotion, since the zebra's face is hidden.
bottleneck: Not-attacking is an absence, and the picture shows no visible reason or hint.
action: Hypothesis: add one small clue near the zebra, such as a pair of watchful eyes in the grass, to test whether a hint raises curiosity.
counterexample: Seq 12 shows a predator in a friendly, bright setting with a person engaging it.

text: THE SECRET / WAS LOST? [no badge or logo text]
scene: On a beach by blue water, a stick-figure Roman-style builder in a cream tunic and dark hair pours brown mortar from a bowl into a stone box standing partly in the sea. Beside him sits a grey concrete cube with a large diagonal crack, and a worried hard-hatted worker in a blue shirt with a yellow helmet holds a clipboard and a pen at the right.

composition: The builder and the stone box form the left cluster, the cracked cube sits at centre and the clipboard worker at the right edge. Eyes travel left to right across three objects. The horizon splits sky and sea, with moderate scene density.
typography: Four words across the top in yellow capitals with a black outline; legible at 160x90. The text adds the lost secret framing and the title adds the ancient technologies angle.
colors: Pale blue sky, deeper sea blue and beige sand with a yellow headline and a yellow hard hat. Grey cube and brown mortar are the muted focal objects.
psychology: The builder's focused frown signals competence while the hard-hatted worker's wide-eyed worry signals alarm. The crack adds a failure cue that quietly flatters the ancient method.
partnership: The title asks which ancient technologies have been lost, and the thumbnail shows one candidate in the form of underwater mortar, hinting at Roman concrete without naming it. The secret itself stays unrevealed.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow THE SECRET WAS LOST? first, then the mortar being poured, then the cracked cube, then the worried hard-hat worker.
art: Flat vector with a slightly textured finish and clean outlines. Scale is coherent, the mortar stream and crack are clearly drawn, and the background is calm, so the scene survives at 160x90.

weakness: The scene needs reading to decode and no object is visually dominant.
bottleneck: Three similarly sized subjects share attention and none clearly leads.

text: THIS HAPPENS / WHEN YOU DRINK / CLOVE WATER
scene: A split frame. On the left a torso of a person with a bare belly, light blue top and jeans carries an overlaid drawing of a pink large intestine packed with brown granular waste. On the right a glass mug of water holds many floating clove buds, with extra cloves scattered on a copper-brown surface. The words sit in a yellow-and-white block top left and a red rounded label top right.
mechanism: A bloated belly with an overlaid waste-packed gut next to a cup of clove water frames the drink as the cause of a dramatic internal change, with the reveal withheld in the word THIS.
composition: Two equal halves are split down the middle, with the belly on the left and the mug on the right. The text block at the top left and the red label at the top right keep a consistent top band. The mug is the strongest focal point with its dense clove detail, while the gut overlay dominates the left.
typography: Seven words across three lines in yellow, white and red-label styling; THIS HAPPENS is the largest and is legible at 160x90 while CLOVE WATER stays readable in its red pill. The title adds Doctors Are Shocked and Senior Health Tips.
colors: Warm copper-brown and amber tones with saturated red label and pink intestine accents, and yellow type for urgency. The red pill labels the product and the pink gut signals the body area.
psychology: The visible bloat and packed gut provoke disgust and fear of internal buildup, while THIS HAPPENS withholds the outcome. No face is shown; the cue is the body itself.
partnership: The title promises doctors are shocked and that clove water does THIS to your body, and the thumbnail pictures the this as a waste-packed gut. It duplicates the phrase and shows no clinical evidence or doctor.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: yellow THIS HAPPENS first, then the packed intestine on the belly, then the red CLOVE WATER pill, then the clove-filled mug.
art: Photoreal torso with a flat vector-style intestine graphic pasted over it; the intestine sits on the belly without matching the skin shading, a visible composite mismatch. The mug image is a polished render with strong glass highlights and a dense texture.
strength: The product name is in a clear red pill and the cause-effect pairing is easy to parse.
weakness: An unqualified body-change claim and an overlaid graphic suggest a result with no evidence.
bottleneck: Gut graphic and cloves compete as two strong focal zones.
action: Hypothesis: replace the packed-waste overlay with a neutral question mark over the belly to test a less alarming, still curious framing.
counterexample: Seq 3 shows a plain topic headline from named physicians with no body imagery.
medical_notes: A drink is shown causing a graphic packed-colon effect on a bloated belly with no clinical evidence, and the title cites shocked doctors that the image never shows.
